archetype.name: Dual-Threat (power runner, vertical passer)
archetype.definition: A big-armed, 237-pound quarterback whose value comes from chunk throws downfield and from being his offense's short-yardage and goal-line runner, with the turnovers that come with that aggression.

report.headline: Deep shots and goal-line runs carry him; the passing has sagged lately.
report.take:
Allen is still the quarterback he has been for six years: a high-variance downfield thrower who doubles as Buffalo's most reliable short-yardage runner. His 0.157 EPA per dropback ranks 11th, 0.184 above the qualifier average, and his 8.37 yards per attempt ranks 7th. His 9 interceptions rank 48th of 55 at the other end. That mix is not new. He threw 15, 14 and 18 interceptions from 2021 to 2023 while posting top-15 EPA every year. The picks are the bill for the style, not a sign of decline.

The passing engine this year is the deep ball. On throws of 20+ air yards he is completing only 38.8%, yet those 49 attempts carry 0.534 EPA apiece and add up to 26.2 EPA, more than his 131 short throws. He is pushing the ball more than last year (aggressiveness up 1.9 points, intended air yards 8.85), and that explains both the higher yards per attempt and a completion rate down 5.1 points. On the ground, 9 of his 11 rushing touchdowns came on designed runs that average just 2.53 yards but succeed 69.4% of the time. He is the goal-line back, and that role is what holds his 23.5 PPR a game at 2nd among quarterbacks.

The 5-0 run hides how ordinary the passing has been lately. Over Weeks 9-11 his EPA per dropback fell to 0.019, his CPOE ran 5.2 points below his season mark, and he threw 4 interceptions in three games. Week 11 against Miami, a 16.5-point favorite, ended at -1.5 passing EPA on 45 attempts. The rushing volume has also faded to 6.7 yards a game over that stretch, though two short touchdown plunges against the Jets propped up the fantasy line. The red zone is a real passing problem: -0.087 EPA, 42.9% completions and a CPOE of -14.7. His scoring there comes on his legs, not his arm.

The outlook is still strong, because the underlying skills held across eight seasons and his team leans on a run game ranked 2nd in EPA. But this is a quarterback winning on chunk plays and goal-line keepers right now, not on down-to-down efficiency. The three-week slump against Minnesota, a soft Jets defense and Miami looks more like scattered accuracy than a structural problem. It still needs to turn before the deep shots get harder to come by in December weather.

strengths.title: Vertical passing pays for itself
strengths.body: His 10+ air-yard throws produce 0.391 EPA per attempt and 43.4 total EPA, with a CPOE of 5.6, so he is hitting tight downfield windows at a rate above expectation, not just heaving. The low deep completion rate and the interceptions are the price, and the EPA says the trade is clearly worth it. This has been his profile his whole career, so it should last, weather permitting.

strengths.title: Goal-line and scramble value
strengths.body: Designed runs rarely gain much but almost always do their job, and nine of them have ended in touchdowns. When plays break down, his 20 scrambles average 0.933 EPA and produced 13 first downs. The scrambling is a durable skill. The touchdown count on designed runs depends on red-zone trips and is running hotter than a role this size usually yields.

strengths.title: Sacks back under control
strengths.body: Last year 40.4% of his pressures became sacks, 47th of 62. That is down to 31% this season, and his sack rate sits 1.3 points better than the league average. He is getting the ball out of trouble more often without giving up the extended plays, which looks like a return to his 2020-2024 norm rather than luck.

concerns.title: Three-week dip in passing efficiency
concerns.body: Weeks 9-11 brought 0.019 EPA per dropback, a CPOE of -3.7 and an interception rate of 4.1%. Wins over Minnesota, the Jets and Miami covered it up. Some of it is a top defense (Minnesota ranks 1st), but the Miami game was bad against a weak unit. His bad-throw rate has been erratic for years, so a short slump fits his variance. It is not yet a trend, but it needs watching.

concerns.title: Red-zone passing stalls
concerns.body: Inside the 20 his passing turns negative: 42.9% completions and a CPOE of -14.7. Buffalo has leaned on his legs instead. That works while the keepers keep scoring, but it makes his touchdown output more dependent on a rushing role that has thinned lately.

concerns.title: Turnovers are part of the package
concerns.body: Nine interceptions in ten games ranks 48th of 55, and the deep and middle-of-the-field throws account for most of them. Given his 18-interception 2023 and similar years, this is who he is rather than bad luck. Expect the pick rate to stay above league average while the aggressive approach keeps paying.

trend.note: His passing EPA peaked in Weeks 1-2 and has trickled down, with Weeks 9-11 his least efficient stretch. His rushing yardage has dropped sharply since Week 5's 121-yard game, though goal-line touchdowns keep his fantasy floor intact.

nextGame.headline: Snow, gusts and a top-five defense squeeze his deep game
nextGame.body:
Kansas City's defense ranks 5th in EPA and 2nd against short throws (-0.14 EPA). That takes away the underneath game where Allen is merely average. The opening is deep: the Chiefs rank 18th in deep EPA, allowing 0.396, which lines up with his best weapon. They also generate little pressure (28th in hit rate, 25th in sack rate), so he should have time. The problem is the forecast for Thursday in Buffalo: snow showers at 98% with 0.34 inches and gusts to 27 mph. That is exactly the weather that clips the deep ball and pushes a run-leaning offense further toward the ground, against a defense 2nd against the run. Quarterbacks have managed only 12.2 PPR a game against KC (3rd stingiest) and 0.8 touchdowns, the fewest in the league.

Availability cuts both ways. Dalton Kincaid is listed out with a thumb injury. He was Allen's most valuable high-volume target at 0.447 EPA per target, and KC gives up above-average production to lead tight ends, so his absence removes the one clean mismatch. Guard O'Cyrus Torrence (100% of snaps) and tackle Spencer Brown (91%) are both questionable on four days' rest, which matters for the interior runs and keepers. On the other side, KC is without guard Trey Smith, tackle Jaylon Moore and running back Kenneth Walker III. That should dent a pass-heavy offense ranked 5th in EPA and help Buffalo, a 3-point favorite, play a controlled, lower-scoring game.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots versus the wind
keyMatchups.body: KC is vulnerable deep, and that is where Allen makes most of his passing value. Gusts near 27 mph in snow make those throws far less reliable, so the shots he does take carry more interception risk than usual.

keyMatchups.title: Underneath game against a wall
keyMatchups.body: KC is 2nd against short passes, and Allen's throws under 10 air yards are his weakest area by EPA. With Kincaid out and the weather limiting depth, Buffalo may have to grind out drives on low-value throws.

keyMatchups.title: Goal-line keepers keep the floor
keyMatchups.body: KC is stingy against the run, but Allen's designed runs win on sheer short-yardage success rather than big gains. In a snowy, red-zone-heavy game, his legs remain the likeliest path to a touchdown.

nextGame.watch: How many true deep attempts Buffalo dials up in the gusts, and whether Allen gets his designed-run carries back near the goal line.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts that last are the vertical accuracy, the scrambling and the short-yardage role in a run-leaning offense. Those have held up across his career and support top-12 passing efficiency from here. The parts likely to cool are the rushing-touchdown rate, which is running well above what his shrinking carry volume normally yields, and the touchdown spike in the 19-play no-huddle sample. His interception rate should stay elevated because that is his style.

Expect roughly 230-265 passing yards a game with around one and a half touchdowns, and rushing yardage closer to his recent levels than his September spike. December weather in Buffalo is the biggest threat to the deep game. Fantasy output should settle near 18-23 PPR a game, still strong but carried a bit less by touchdowns.
swingFactors: Whether designed-run volume near the goal line returns
Kincaid's thumb and the offensive line's health

confidence.note: Long, stable career profile, but the recent slump, the role shift on the ground and Thursday's snow add variance.
